01.r: The sheep and goats each family keeps.
01.n: Gesenius: a collective noun, flocks, small cattle, that is, sheep and goats. It is singular in form, 'your flock', and stands first for emphasis, as 'your seed' does in 1 Samuel 8:15.

s: he will take a tenth of
he will take the tithe of
02.r: The king will take one tenth of the flock for himself.
02.n: Gesenius: to decimate, that is, to take the tenth part of produce, to tithe, citing this verse and 1 Sa. 8:15; this plain form means to take the tenth, while another form means to give it. So the tithing here is the king's taking.

03.r: After the produce, the people themselves.
03.n: The pronoun is written out, for emphasis: not only your goods, but you. The BSB shows this with 'you yourselves'.

04.r: What they will become under the king.

05.r: They will belong to the king.
05.n: Literally 'to him', the Hebrew way of saying 'his'.

06.r: The whole people will be the king's slaves.
06.n: Gesenius: a servant, among the Hebrews commonly a slave, and he notes the word is applied to a whole people when subject and tributary to another. Here the whole people, not court officials, so 'slaves', as in the BSB. Literally 'for slaves', as YLT has it.

_extra.0: καὶ (and): added by the Greek translators; nothing in the Hebrew answers to it.

01.n: ποίμνιον, flock, plural in the Greek.

02.n: ἀποδεκατόω, to tithe, take a tenth: the same verb the Greek uses in 1 Samuel 8:15.
